page: Microsoft Azure FX48mds_v2 is a memory-optimized server instance built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 1008.0 GB of RAM, providing 21.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a 2835 GB NVMe SSD. The CPU architecture is x86_64, incorporating advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 330.82 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 158.98 GB/sec. Single-core performance is highlighted by a Geekbench score of 2338.0, placing it in the top tier, while multi-core performance registers a Geekbench score of 20347.0. In database operations, the server achieves 74.99 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a PassMark database score of 28908.89. For computational workloads, the instance processes 2674.21 tokens per second for small LLM prompt processing and achieves 337.81 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The FX48mds_v2 offers high resource density, combining a large memory footprint with fast local NVMe storage. This profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive memory-to-CPU ratios without the overhead of multi-node clustering. However, the lack of a dedicated GPU limits its efficiency for heavy deep learning training, though the integrated Intel AMX instructions provide capable CPU-based LLM inference. This server is suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
